overall_summary: Performance analysis across the deduplicated dataset clearly demonstrates that high-concept space scenarios and bizarre planetary mechanics ('What if' and extreme environment hooks) dramatically outperform standard biological or psychological facts. Videos focusing on hypothetical planetary falls (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice) and extreme cosmic phenomena (e.g., Venus's day/year ratio, TrES-2b, supersonic ruby rain) are driving the highest views-per-day and stronger likes-per-view ratios. Conversely, older, straightforward psychology or basic animal trivia have plateaued with low engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) show sustained high velocity and superior engagement compared to static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space 'what-if' scenarios involving bizarre physics, exotic materials, and planetary survival hazards.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal conditions such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) and 'This Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,027 views) capture top-tier viewership within the recent 7-day window.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into extreme exoplanet meteorology, bizarre orbital mechanics, and lesser-known cosmic extremes.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic animal facts (e.g., 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' posted multiple times or older shark/brain facts) yield stagnant views and lower like ratios over time.
weak_patterns.action: Shift away from basic animal/psychology facts unless framed within a completely fresh, high-stakes cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary paradox narrative.

weak_patterns.evidence: Directly repeating or slightly rewording identical space facts ('Why Space Is Completely Silent') across multiple upload dates results in diminishing returns (35 views on recent drops).
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness checks against the published history to prevent audience fatigue and algorithm suppression.
